generation_capture.final_message: Both claims express least-element principles. `Nat.find p` is the smallest natural satisfying `p`, so \(n\) lies below it exactly when no \(m<n\) satisfies \(p\). Likewise, Chebyshev’s \(\theta(x)\) sums \(\log p\) over primes \(p\le x\); since every prime is at least \(2\), the sum is empty when \(x<2\), hence zero.
